architecture_decisions: - **Canonical Project ID**: The client must not send a `Project.id` that is not the current owner-scoped Project list or the canonical `Project.id` from the protected `/v1/projects` API.
work_items: - **Code conversation creation**: The client must not create a Code conversation with a `Project.id` that is not the current owner-scoped Project list or the canonical `Project.id` from the protected `/v1/projects` API.
validations: - **Project selection**: The client must not select a `Project.id` that is not the current owner-scoped Project list or the canonical `Project.id` from the protected `/v1/projects` API.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — After authenticated workspace initialization, the client loads Projects through `GET /v1/projects` using the existing authenticated transport. The typed Project contract carries canonical `id`, display name/slug, optional repository metadata and status without using `workspace_ref` as execution authority.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Project selection is explicit and deterministic. A selected ID must resolve to the current owner-scoped Project list; stale/missing IDs are cleared. If exactly one valid Project exists, the client may select it automatically for convenience, but it may never invent or infer a Project from repository/workspace metadata.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — The Code-mode Project surface can create a Project through `POST /v1/projects` with required bounded name plus optional bounded `repository_ref`, preserving current backend validation/conflict semantics. On success the server-returned canonical Project is added to the list and selected. Failure does not create a local synthetic Project.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Every new Code conversation created from mode switching, NEW conversation, or first-message bootstrap calls the existing conversation API with `mode: "code"` and the currently selected canonical `project_id`. Code creation is blocked locally when no valid Project is selected and never retries as unbound.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Reason conversation creation, mode switching to Reason, response streaming and existing conversation history behavior remain unchanged and do not require a Project selection. No Project-selection state may alter Reason Work Specification or response behavior.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Opening a historical Code conversation with `project_binding_status == "HISTORICAL_UNBOUND"` remains supported and presents a concise compatibility indication. The client does not mutate, rebind, or silently assign that conversation to the currently selected Project.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Project list/create failures, stale selection and backend missing/removed/cross-owner Project failures surface bounded user-visible error state without retry loops. Authentication expiry preserves the existing private-session lock behavior. No failure path sends unbound Code creation.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — The selector/create surface reuses the existing Parallax palette, type hierarchy, controls and interaction language. Desktop and 390x844-class mobile browser acceptance proves no regression to safe-area/composer clearance, live-edge behavior, mode controls, Work Specification status, Engineering Run controls or core conversation geometry.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Focused deterministic tests prove selection validity, stale-selection clearing, single-Project auto-selection behavior, canonical Code creation payload, Reason payload preservation and failure-to-unbound denial. Browser acceptance proves Project list/select/create and successful canonical Code creation at desktop and 390x844-class mobile, plus representative API failure behavior.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The candidate contains this approved specification, authentic committed DSPy compiled plan, only the minimum declared client compatibility implementation/tests, exact validation evidence, and an open PR targeting `integration/wave2-app-builder`. Workstream Spec Validation, Parallax P2 CI, Bounded Autonomy Pilot, backend API regression, client typecheck/state/export and browser acceptance are green. The worker does not merge, deploy, edit authoritative records, or broaden into dashboard/product redesign scope.
risks: - **Client-side compatibility**: The backend Project requirement must not be weakened.
